title: STORY TIME: My entire diet history
summary: NH tells his diet history: five years of eating whatever his parents served (110 to 170 lb), a year of Subway in a US dorm, chicken-rice-spinach while broke, a dirty bulk up to 240 lb with injuries, then a slow cut to 210 and a recomp after removing dairy, eggs and red meat. His lesson is that nutrition matters less than training for gains but most for health and longevity.
claims: NH made more diet mistakes than training mistakes over his lifting career
For novices diet barely matters unless they're very skinny or very fat; eat what your parents give you, as much as you can, and train
Novices lack the work capacity to train much at first
In his first five years NH ate without tracking, supplements or knowing macros and went from 110 to about 170 lb
As you train and grow, appetite rises; the body asks for the fuel it needs
NH ate less protein than most prescribe early on and still grew, so stop worrying about optimising diet, especially as a beginner
NH believes he gained the most lean mass during the slow years of eating slightly above maintenance
If possible, live off campus; dorms with no kitchen and overpriced cafeterias make gaining very hard
In the US at 20 he ate two foot-long Subway subs (about 1,200 kcal each) plus soup daily, around 3,000 kcal, and gained fast
Novices on strength programs while bulking get infatuated with bench gains but put on less muscle than they think
Cook for yourself; it's cheapest, and grown men should be able to feed themselves
While broke he ate only chicken breast, white rice, spinach and olives, about six meals a day, for a full year
His dirty bulk included 12 eggs a day, pounds of beef and pounds of spaghetti bolognese
Force-feeding makes huge intake the new normal, which is not good for the body
Chasing strength to get bigger, he went from 210 to 240 lb at 22-23, mostly fat, and was injury prone; his ribs wouldn't heal
Eating far above what the body needs for muscle just produces fat
From 23 to 25 he crashed to 210, rebounded to 225, then slowly dropped to 210 with large body composition improvements
After advice based on his genetic makeup, he cut milk, dairy and most eggs and red meat; within six months water retention and fat dropped and he felt more anabolic and pain-free
Training is the variable that drives growth, but food and calories matter most for longevity and health
